name: What hidden costs surprise people when building a custom home in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What hidden costs usually surprise people during single-family home construction in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What hidden costs usually surprise people during single-family home construction in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden costs often come from site conditions and design changes rather than the structure itself. In Los Angeles-area projects, grading, export hauling, retaining walls, soil reports, utility trenching, sewer line upgrades, and stormwater requirements can add major cost. On the soft-cost side, homeowners often underestimate architecture revisions, engineering, permit fees, school or utility connection charges, and extended carrying costs if the schedule slips. Finish allowances are another common trap: flooring, cabinetry, windows, appliances, lighting, and fixtures can move the budget quickly if the allowance is too low. Change orders are especially expensive once framing and systems are underway. A good budget should include a contingency reserve and a clearly defined allowance schedule before construction begins. The safest way to avoid surprises is to complete due diligence on the lot early and lock the scope, materials, and specifications before breaking ground.
acceptedAnswer.description: The most common surprise costs are grading, hauling soil, utility trenching, retaining walls, sewer and water upgrades, plan revisions, inspection delays, and higher-end finish allowances. Owners also underestimate temporary power, fencing, protection of neighboring properties, and change orders after construction starts.
